title: Comparing Make.com Pricing 2026 Plans and Real Costs
summary: Make.com pricing depends on your monthly operation volume, allowing you to select the tier that aligns with your specific automation requirements.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs of operation-based automation billing


Operation-based billing models transform every logical step of a workflow into a metered expense. This often decouples the value of an automation from its monthly cost.


> Operation-based billing models transform every logical step of a workflow into a metered expense.


### How operations are actually counted


In a metered environment like Make.com, an "operation" is consumed every time a module performs a task. This happens regardless of whether that task successfully moves data.


This includes every search that returns no results, every filter that stops a bundle, and every error handler that triggers to keep a scenario running.


A single execution of a complex workflow can consume dozens of operations. The consequence for you is a "complexity tax" where robust error handling and multi-branch logic directly accelerate the consumption of the prepaid tier.


### How loop iterations drain Make.com credits


While internal logic steps are often the focus, the most significant hidden cost arises from iterative processing. If you use a 'Loop' or 'Foreach' step to process a list, **every single iteration counts** as an additional task or run against your quota.


A flow that imports a 100-row CSV does not cost one credit; it costs at least 100 credits because each row is treated as a distinct operation.


This behavior is standard across most automation platforms and can quickly deplete a monthly allowance during bulk data migrations.


Pricing that rises with granularity punishes the exact discipline good automation depends on, which is why MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The meter is the run, not the steps inside it; the published pricing page shows 1 credit per flow run regardless of whether the flow contains two steps or twenty, so you are incentivized to build complex, multi-stage workflows without incurring additional usage fees.


This ensures that building reliable, multi-step logic doesn't increase the cost of a single execution.


### The price of data transfer limits


Beyond the count of operations, platforms often impose caps on the total volume of data moved within a billing cycle.


When a workflow uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 to process large PDF transcripts, the size of those payloads can trigger data transfer ceilings before the operation count is exhausted. Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a model designed for balanced speed and intelligence.


Reaching these limits typically results in the immediate suspension of all active scenarios.


### Calculating the cost of high-frequency polling


Polling-based triggers create a constant drain on operation quotas because they must execute on a schedule to check for new information.


While a Webhook-based trigger only consumes an operation when an event actually occurs, a polling trigger checking an inbox or database every few minutes will consume thousands of operations per month.


- A Webhook: is event-driven and only runs when data is sent, resulting in low cost impact.
- Polling: is schedule-driven and runs at fixed intervals, resulting in high quota depletion regardless of activity.


To maintain low latency without exhausting a budget, you're frequently pushed toward higher-tier plans.
